observation: Header block is a company profile: founder, name, stage, business type (Canadian C Corp), team size, founding year, funding to date, industry, TAM, 5-yr market share, exit multiple
implication: Pairs entities need a profile section beyond name/currency/accounts; same fields useful for speculative companies

observation: KPIs sit in groups (Core Business, Product User, Biz Dev & Traction, Fundraising) as monthly columns: starting column + Month 1..6
implication: Model as metric definitions (with bucket) plus monthly values; the first column becomes the optional starting/current month

observation: Groups mix ledger numbers (revenue, COGS, burn), derived ratios (ARR, margins, LTV:CAC, CAC payback) and founder/product activity counts (investor connections, meetings, conversions, LOIs, NPS)
implication: Each metric needs a source type: ledger / derived / manual; only manual ones need entry forms

observation: Rows 80-111 are free-form custom metrics: audience (newsletter, open rate, CTR, press), funnel (MQL, SQL, cost per lead, signups) and product-specific app statistics
implication: Users must add their own metrics into buckets; built-in catalogue is a starting point

observation: Deck, one-pager and data room are links, not numbers
implication: Profile needs a links/documents list

observation: Month header dates have typos (2021-01 and 2021-03 should be 2022); burn entered by hand
implication: Generate period headers; never type dates per column

observation: Model settings: company, currency, first forecast month, fiscal year end, beginning cash
implication: Pairs already knows currency and fiscal start; beginning cash can come from the real bank balance

observation: Cap table inputs are 4 numbers: founding shares, founder %, % sold per round, option pool % per round
implication: Too simple for real use; a dedicated cap-table tool with holders and versions is needed

observation: Burn & Runway: begin/end cash, net burn, breakeven flag, average burn, cash at end of month 1
implication: Standalone report that can run on manual inputs or ledger actuals (plus scenario for future months)

observation: Summarized cost budget by quarter by 5 categories (Salaries; Ads & Marketing; Product & Materials; Legal & Accounting; Overhead)
implication: Needs a mapping from ledger accounts to reporting categories

observation: Sources & Uses: raise $X to last N months, split by category %
implication: Raise planner: given runway target and budget mix -> raise size; ties to scenarios

observation: Traction & Ownership chart: chosen traction metric vs founder ownership vs cash over time
implication: Good investor-facing combined view once metrics and cap table exist

observation: Revenue streams and ~30 expense lines, each tagged with a category; months copy forward (=previous)
implication: Same as scenario items with frequencies; "copy forward" = monthly repeat

observation: Expenses by stage bands (Startup / Seed / Growth date ranges)
implication: Optional period bands (stages) for reports

observation: Cash detail separates revenues, expenses and financing inflows: equity/convertible/SAFE, debt, grants
implication: Scenarios need non-P&L cash inflow items so runway is right

observation: CAC block: % of each category allocated to acquisition, then CAC, LTV, LTV/CAC (CAC and LTV still typed by hand)
implication: Allocation % per category + customers acquired metric = computed CAC

observation: Form of Investment & Conversion: each round splits into equity vs new convertible notes; outstanding notes carried; at next priced round they convert using discount %, valuation cap and monthly interest (FV); conversion price = min(round price x (1-discount), cap price); premoney method only
implication: Instrument terms must be per instrument (note/SAFE) not per round; support pre-money note math and post-money SAFE

observation: Investment Rounds & Cap Table: % sold -> post-money = investment / % sold, pre = post - investment; price = pre / shares at start; new shares = investment/price + converted/conversion price; option pool topped up to target % post-money; fully diluted adds unconverted notes at cap
implication: Core round math to reproduce; per-holder detail and share classes missing

observation: Ownership: founders+options vs investors as shares, %, $ value at last price, $ invested
implication: Version comparison output: dilution and value per holder group

observation: Template limits: two holder groups only, options treated as common, no per-holder rows, no liquidation preference, no pro-rata
implication: Pairs version should be per holder and per class but stay simple to enter

observation: Model errors: a round typed into the cap-table row but not the cash row (Sources & Uses breaks, cash goes negative); % sold left empty so cap table never computes; CAC allocation mixes fractions and whole percents; net burn typed with the wrong sign
implication: Enter a funding event once and derive both cash and cap table; validate units (% vs fraction)

observation: Standalone round table: columns by investor class (founders, friends & family, angel/seed, Series A-D, options); per round: investment, added common, preferred, options; cumulative shares by type; price = pre-money / prior shares; post = pre + investment
implication: Core executive view; extends cap table with investor classes and share types

observation: Classic 3-statement flow: assumptions -> personnel by department -> income statement -> balance sheet -> cash flow -> debt and credit line -> summary -> cost of capital -> DCF valuation
implication: Gives the narrative "portrait": each section reads from the one above it; Pairs can show actual statements from the books and projected ones from scenarios

observation: Drivers: interest on cash and debt, tax rates, days sales/payables/inventory outstanding (working capital), useful life (depreciation), equipment cost per new hire, minimum cash = N months of payroll
implication: Assumptions block per scenario; working-capital days and min-cash policy matter once operating

observation: Credit line (revolver) draws automatically to keep minimum cash and repays when cash allows; tax loss carryforward; balance-sheet check and checksum
implication: Useful safeguards; balance check is free in Pairs because the books are double-entry

observation: Revenue driven by revenue per business-development employee and per salesperson (sales capacity model)
implication: One of several growth models; links hiring to revenue

observation: Valuation by cost of capital (WACC) and DCF; the sheet itself notes this is arbitrary for early-stage firms; file has broken references (circular credit line, #REF summary, DCF pointing at missing rows)
implication: Low priority; for early stage, VC method, comparables or scorecard methods fit better

observation: Paid channel: per source impressions x CTR = clicks x conversion = signups; CPA = spend / signups. Funnel: bought users grow with ad spend %, viral users = previous new users x viral factor (invites x invite conversion), free-to-paid conversion
implication: A growth engine: channels produce new users per period, then a shared funnel converts them

observation: Cohort matrix: each period's new users decay by a retention rate (attrition over time, separate for paying and all users); LTV = revenue per paying user x sum of retained user-periods / cohort size
implication: Retention is a stock that decays, not a monthly flow; LTV should be derived from it (the sheet's LTV only covers the first cohort)

observation: Revenue mix by tier (average revenue x share of payers) = revenue per paying user; cost of service per user; result = revenue - ad spend - cost of service (what is left for operations)
implication: Not a separate sheet in Pairs; becomes the contribution-after-acquisition line of the growth report

observation: Per product line: units sold, unit price, unit COGS, margin per unit, growth rate per line, a retention factor on units, cumulative profit after expenses
implication: Per-unit revenue lines = I03 per-unit items; growth per line = I04

observation: MRR movements by month: new, expansion (upgrades), contraction, churn; active customers (sample vendor data)
implication: MRR bridge is a standard derived metric set once revenue is recurring

observation: Roles grouped by department with salary, start and end month and raise %; monthly cost appears only between start and end
implication: Confirms the hiring-plan design (I05)

observation: Sheets are mostly separate templates; only the growth chain (acquisition -> funnel -> retention -> cashflow -> LTV) is linked. Model revenue does not come from the funnel; hiring plan is separate from Model personnel
implication: Pairs should connect them once: growth engine -> revenue; hiring -> payroll; both -> scenario -> statements and runway; funding -> cap table

observation: One row per investor: name, email, organization, referral source, investor type, first and last meeting date, round type, status, amount committed, next steps/notes
implication: An investor pipeline (CRM) for fundraising; investor is a contact plus a deal per round

observation: Dropdowns: status stages 1st call > 2nd call > due diligence > documents requested > soft committed > agreement sent > signed > capital received; investor types angel (family, pro, super, group), VC, private equity, family office, corporate venture, other; referral source list; round type pre-seed/seed/Series A/bridge/other
implication: Default stage, investor-type and round-type lists; configurable per company

observation: Guidance: log every conversation even when it ends, so those investors get progress updates later (creates FOMO and later investment)
implication: Keep closed/declined investors as an updates audience; investor update list

observation: Investor, amount, closed date, round type; list current soft and hard circled commitments as well as history
implication: Commitment = pipeline stage; closing creates the funding event (cash) and the share issuance (cap table)

observation: Round name, round type, instrument (convertible note, equity, SAFE, other), round amount, anticipated close date
implication: A shared Round object used by the pipeline, cap table versions and scenario funding items

observation: Raise target = average projected burn next quarter x buffer months (15, not 12), because founders underestimate costs and build time by about a third; aim for runway well beyond the estimated time to profitability
implication: Raise calculator with an editable buffer and the reason shown; fits next to Sources & Uses

observation: Pipeline counts (connections, meetings, conversions) are what the KPI tracker asked founders to type by hand
implication: Founder-momentum metrics can be counted from the pipeline instead of typed
